Explicitly terminating that launcher still left containers requiring project-scoped cleanup. content.text:
Astra found no later lifecycle fix on current main. The original log had reached test execution, so it does not establish that cancellation occurred inside global setup.

The signal distinction also matters: Playwright watches for inbound SIGINT, while its webserver SIGTERM setting controls outbound shutdown of the launcher. Astra is checking that boundary in the reproduction.

The investigation now has a clean worktree based on current main, tracked in [EVO-102](https://linear.app/evorto/issue/EVO-102/clean-up-disposable-playwright-stacks-when-the-runner-is-interrupted) and [Trail 39](https://entire.com/gh/evorto-app/-/trails/39). Reproduction will use task-owned Compose projects and unique loopback ports.

The isolated reproduction confirmed the leak on current main: SIGTERM to the actual Playwright CLI during PostgreSQL global setup exited the runner, but after 6.48 seconds the launcher still held its lease and the containers, network, and volume remained.

The separate persistent fixture kept its container and volume IDs and SQL marker. Astra is testing a repair at the runner’s cancellation boundary.

The trial fix passed the same probe: routing the runner’s first SIGTERM through Playwright’s existing SIGINT cancellation path completed cleanup in 2.58 seconds. The lease could be reacquired and the port rebound; the separate persistent database and its resource identities were unchanged.

Astra is turning this into a focused change with regression tests. The result will stay local for review unless the full publication checks are satisfied.

The before-and-after probe has established the leak and a working cleanup path. The remaining work is durable regression coverage and checking that the signal handler applies only to the Playwright runner, without changing app or deployment processes.
